title: Grateful Dead Live at Onondaga County War Memorial on 1973-09-17

ai_review.summary: Soundboard recording with good clarity captures a unique 1973 second set where horns join the Dead on Wake of the Flood material and an electrifying Weather Report Suite.
ai_review.review: The tape is a sound‑board source that sounds clean enough for most listeners, though a few note the hall’s poor acoustics. Musically the show stands out for the surprise horn section (Martin Fierro) backing several Wake of the Flood numbers and an energetic Weather Report Suite, with Keith's jam on Truckin' getting special praise. Opinions on the horns are split, making the overall reception mixed.

ai_rating.rationale: Average star rating of ~4 across 14 reviews; strong positive comments about the unique horn‑enhanced second set and decent soundboard quality, offset by a minority who disliked the horns.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Generally clear and well‑balanced; no major dropouts mentioned. One reviewer noted the venue’s hall sound was terrible, but that refers to live acoustics rather than the tape itself.

standout_songs: Wake of the Flood material (e.g., songs from the album)
show_quality.setlist_flow: Second set is the highlight, featuring an unexpected horn section that adds a jazzy flavor to Wake of the Flood tunes and carries through into the Weather Report Suite. The horns divide listeners—some love the energy, others feel they detract from classic Dead moments.

band_member_comments.Jerry: One reviewer noted Jerry sings a line from "Sugar Magnolia"; another wished guitars were louder.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith's jam on Truckin' is praised for its energy, and his vocal moment on an obscure tune is highlighted as a fun surprise.
